reference.source: ATS/ERS interstitial lung disease guidance and respiratory genetics texts
clinicalPearls: Consider in a term newborn with severe unexplained respiratory distress and diffuse infiltrates that fails to resolve like typical prematurity-related disease
Surfactant protein B and ABCA3 deficiency typically present in the neonatal period, often with rapidly progressive and severe disease
Surfactant protein C mutations and some ABCA3 variants can present later in childhood or in adults as chronic interstitial lung disease
Inheritance differs by gene: SFTPB and ABCA3 are autosomal recessive, whereas SFTPC disease is autosomal dominant and may arise de novo
High-resolution imaging shows diffuse ground-glass change and, over time, features of chronic interstitial lung disease
Genetic testing has largely replaced lung biopsy as the confirmatory investigation where the phenotype is suggestive
Family history of neonatal death or childhood interstitial lung disease supports a heritable surfactant disorder
reference.pathophysiology: Pulmonary surfactant lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse. Mutations in SFTPB and SFTPC (encoding surfactant proteins B and C) or in ABCA3 (a lipid transporter required for surfactant assembly and packaging within lamellar bodies of type II pneumocytes) impair production, processing, or secretion of functional surfactant. The resulting surfactant dysfunction causes alveolar instability, impaired gas exchange, and accumulation of abnormal proteinaceous and lipid material, driving neonatal respiratory failure or a chronic fibrosing interstitial lung disease depending on the gene and specific variant.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital pulmonary alveolar proteinosis from CSF2 receptor defects
Other childhood interstitial lung diseases (for example NKX2-1 related disease)
Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of SFTPB, SFTPC and ABCA3
Echocardiography to assess for pulmonary hypertension and exclude cardiac disease
Infection and sepsis screen to exclude mimics
Lung biopsy with electron microscopy in selected undiagnosed cases
Blood gas analysis and oxygenation assessment
redFlags: Refractory hypoxaemic respiratory failure in a term neonate not responding to standard support
Progressive interstitial lung disease with declining exercise tolerance
Family history of neonatal respiratory death
reference.prognosis: Surfactant protein B and severe ABCA3 deficiency are frequently fatal in infancy without lung transplantation, whereas SFTPC and milder ABCA3 disease follow a more variable chronic course; overall outcome depends heavily on the specific gene and mutation.
pitfalls: Assuming term neonatal respiratory distress is simply delayed transition or infection and missing a genetic surfactant disorder
Overlooking a dominant SFTPC diagnosis because a parent has mild or subclinical lung disease
Attributing later-onset interstitial lung disease solely to environmental causes
Delaying transplant referral in severe neonatal forms
references: American Thoracic Society statement on childhood interstitial lung disease
Standard respiratory medicine and paediatric pulmonology texts
management: Tailor definitive management to the gene: lung transplantation for severe neonatal surfactant protein B and ABCA3 deficiency, where exogenous surfactant gives only transient benefit
Trial empirical anti-inflammatory therapy such as corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine or azithromycin in the chronic interstitial forms (surfactant protein C and milder ABCA3 disease)
Provide respiratory support with oxygen and mechanical ventilation, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a bridge in refractory neonatal failure
Maintain immunisation, treat intercurrent infection promptly and optimise nutrition and growth
Monitor with serial high-resolution CT, pulmonary function testing and echocardiographic surveillance for pulmonary hypertension
Coordinate care across neonatology or respiratory medicine, an interstitial lung disease service and a transplant centre
Provide genetic counselling and family screening tailored to inheritance (autosomal recessive for SFTPB and ABCA3, autosomal dominant for SFTPC)
